title: Fall back to aten in the RMSNorm override when N exceeds the smem budget
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #186941

Fixes #186800

The CuTe/Quack _fused_rms_norm override accepted arbitrarily large
normalized dims, but the quack kernel splits each row across a CTA
cluster (at most 16) and stages the per-CTA row tile in shared memory.
Rows whose tile cannot fit even at the maximum cluster size can never
launch, and for very large N (e.g. 2^28 from the issue) the CuTe DSL
compiler hangs or crashes before any launch-time smem check could fire.

Bound N in the cond predicates by the device's opt-in shared memory so
oversized rows route to the aten CUDA kernel instead. The bound mirrors
the kernel's actual smem footprint for fwd and bwd, so it admits
everything that can physically launch and adapts to each arch's smem
capacity.

Test Plan

New routing tests in TestFusedRMSNormOverrideRouting cover the issue's
shape (bf16 N=2^28, previously a ~9 minute compiler spin ending in a
segfault, now a sub-second aten call) and both sides of the fwd/bwd
smem boundaries. Numerics verified on both sides of each boundary on
B200.

```
python -m pytest test/test_nn.py -k "FusedRMSNorm"
```

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).
